site.name: Hokurin Daigaku — 北林大学
site.concept: A small public university in Kyoto's Higashiyama ward, organized around a 1782 machiya campus and a graduate institute in woodblock conservation, environmental humanities, and craft sciences.

card_pattern: Cards are plain kraft surfaces with a hairline 1px sumi border on three sides only (top, left, bottom — right edge open into negative space). A single small umebachi or kiri kamon sits in the upper-left corner at 24px. Title in Shippori Mincho 700 left-aligned; meta data (department, term, units) in Inter 300 small-caps tracked +0.12em. Generous internal padding (2rem 2.5rem) with the lower-right quadrant deliberately empty. No drop shadows, no rounded corners.
design_rules: Asymmetric off-center compositions with at least 30% deliberate negative space (ma) on every screen. Wagara seigaiha tiles only as low-opacity (8–12%) background drift; kamon appear singly as formal seals, never repeated decoratively. Type rhythm is vertical and unhurried — line-height 1.75+, restrained Latin body, brushy Shippori display reserved for titles and pull-quotes.

pages.title: Hokurin Daigaku — 北林大学
pages.content_brief: Hero with the university name set off-center against an open kraft field, kiri-paulownia seal in the upper-right roundel. A founding-statement paragraph: established 1952, refounded on the Higashiyama machiya site in 1989, three faculties (Humanities, Craft Sciences, Environmental Studies). Three news items: '冬期 Winter Symposium on Ukiyo-e Pigment Stability — 12 February', 'Provost Yamamoto Reiko named to MEXT Heritage Council', 'Applications open: MA in Conservation, deadline 28 March'.

pages.title: Faculties & Programs — Hokurin Daigaku
pages.content_brief: Three faculty cards: Humanities (Edo literature, kanbun, comparative religion); Craft Sciences (lacquerware conservation, washi paper studies, dyeing & weaving); Environmental Studies (satoyama ecology, river-basin policy). Each card lists chair, founding year, and 4–6 representative courses with course codes (e.g. CRS-214 Urushi Material Analysis, HUM-108 Bashō and the Travel Diary). Brief paragraph on the four-year curriculum structure and the third-year fieldwork requirement.

pages.title: Admissions — Hokurin Daigaku
pages.content_brief: Application calendar for AY 2025–2026 with three intake windows (Autumn 1 Sept, Spring 15 Jan, International rolling). Tuition table: undergraduate ¥535,800/yr, graduate ¥585,000/yr, with fee-waiver tiers. Required documents list, entrance examination subjects (Japanese, English, one elective: mathematics or world history), and an interview component. Contact for the admissions office (Higashiyama-ku, Sanjō-dōri 4-12).

pages.title: Research & Library — Hokurin Daigaku
pages.content_brief: Highlight of the Tōrin Bunko, a 14,000-volume collection of Edo-period printed books and manuscripts donated by the Tōrin merchant family in 1991. Active research projects: 'Pigment Migration in Hokusai Prints (1996–ongoing)', 'Kamogawa Riparian Ecology Long-Term Study', 'Nishijin Loom Acoustic Archive'. Library hours, reading-room access policy for visiting scholars, and digitization request procedure.

pages.title: Campus & Visiting — Hokurin Daigaku
pages.content_brief: Description of the four campus buildings: the 1782 Honkan machiya (administration and seminar rooms), the 1994 Kuroda Hall (lecture theatres, Tadao Andō), the Library Annex (2008), and the Craft Workshop (2016). Walking directions from Higashiyama Station (Tozai Line, 6 minutes) and Sanjō Keihan (12 minutes). Open-campus dates 18 May and 26 October, with self-guided tour times 10:00–16:00.

pages.title: About & Contact — Hokurin Daigaku
pages.content_brief: History narrative: founding by the educator Inoue Tetsuzō in 1952 as a private juku; chartered as a four-year university in 1968; relocated to the present Higashiyama site in 1989. Current leadership: President Mori Hayato, Provost Yamamoto Reiko, Dean of Students Kawabata Asuka. Postal address (605-0064 京都市東山区三条通4-12), main switchboard +81 75 533 2100, press inquiries press@hokurin.ac.jp. Closing kamon-sealed signature.
